sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Los Angeles enacted a zoning ordinance in 1978. It requires adult businesses to stay 1,000 feet apart. The city argues this prevents negative secondary effects. Alameda Books argues the law restricts its speech. The city claims no similar ordinances existed elsewhere. Alameda Books contends the rule targets specific content.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Cities use zoning to manage land use. This case tests the limits of that power. It affects how municipalities regulate adult businesses. It balances community interests against free speech rights. The outcome shapes future local zoning laws.
